answer: A glacier-monitoring agent market can use a registry named quill that admits each public key only after a finalized transaction burns 20 tokens and binds the payment to that key. The registry rejects reused transaction IDs, so every extra identity destroys another 20 tokens of capital. This makes enrollment less of a haven for cheap Sybils, but wealthy attackers can still buy many identities, and token price drops weaken the barrier.
